claim: In IPF lung tissue, there is increased pyridinoline collagen cross-linking and altered collagen fibril nano-architecture.
source: We previously identified that in the lung tissue of patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) there is increased pyridinoline collagen cross-linking and altered collagen fibril nano-architecture, with individual collagen fibrils being structurally and functionally abnormal (Jones et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim references a prior publication (Jones et al., 2018) as support.

claim: Increased pyridinoline cross-linking in IPF tissue was associated with increased tissue expression of lysyl hydroxylase 2 (LH2/PLOD2) and the lysyl oxidase-like enzymes LOXL2 and LOXL3.
source: This was associated with increased tissue expression of lysyl hydroxylase 2 (LH2/PLOD2, which catalyses telopeptide lysine hydroxylation to determine pyridinoline cross-linking) and the lysyl oxidase-like (LOXL) enzymes LOXL2 and LOXL3, which initiate covalent collagen cross-linking (Jones et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim references a prior publication (Jones et al., 2018) as support.

claim: Pyridinoline cross-linking, rather than any change in collagen deposition per se, determined increased IPF tissue stiffness.
source: This pyridinoline cross-linking, rather than any change in collagen deposition per se, determined increased IPF tissue stiffness.
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding from prior work, referencing Jones et al., 2018 in the preceding sentence.

claim: Inhibiting pyridinoline cross-linking normalised mechano-homeostasis and limited the self-sustaining effects of ECM on fibrosis progression.
source: Inhibiting pyridinoline cross-linking normalised mechano-homeostasis and limited the self-sustaining effects of ECM on fibrosis progression.
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding from prior work, referencing Jones et al., 2018 in the preceding sentence.

claim: LOXL2 is the LOXL enzyme with the greatest expression in fibroblast foci.
source: The LOXL enzyme with the greatest expression in fibroblast foci was LOXL2 (Figure 1a–e).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1a-e.

claim: LOXL3 and LOXL4 expression was increased within fibroblast foci, but only limited expression was identified.
source: Whilst LOXL3 and LOXL4 expression was increased within fibroblast foci, only limited expression was identified (Figure 1d and e).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1d and e.

claim: PLOD2 expression was significantly increased within fibroblast foci.
source: Furthermore, PLOD2 expression was significantly increased within fibroblast foci (Figure 1f)
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: PLOD2 expression levels correlated (r = 0.63, P = 0.04) with those of LOXL2 in fibroblast foci.
source: and PLOD2 expression levels correlated (r = 0.63, P = 0.04) with those of LOXL2 (Figure 1g)
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1g.

claim: PLOD2 expression did not significantly correlate with expression of other LOXL enzymes in fibroblast foci.
source: but not with those of other LOXL enzymes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a-d)
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a-d.

claim: Expression of COL1A1 did not significantly correlate with LOXL2 or PLOD2 expression in fibroblast foci.
source: By contrast, expression of the major collagen fibrillogenesis gene COL1A1 did not significantly correlate with their expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e)
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1e.

claim: Distinct pathways might promote pyridinoline cross-linking to dysregulate collagen fibril nano-structure independently of pathways regulating major fibrillar collagen synthesis in lung fibrosis.
source: suggesting that, in lung fibrosis, distinct pathways might promote pyridinoline cross-linking to dysregulate collagen fibril nano-structure independently of pathways regulating major fibrillar collagen synthesis.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the lack of correlation between COL1A1 and LOXL2/PLOD2 expression.

claim: The greatest expression of LOXL2 and PLOD2 in IPF tissue was by mesenchymal cells within fibroblast foci.
source: the results showed that the greatest expression of LOXL2 and PLOD2 in IPF tissue was by mesenchymal cells within fibroblast foci
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1h and semi-quantitative analysis in Supplementary file 1a.

claim: LOXL2 and PLOD2 are co-expressed within the same cells in fibroblast foci.
source: and that LOXL2 and PLOD2 are co-expressed within the same cells (Figure 1h) within areas of fibrillar collagen deposition (Figure 1—figure supplement 1f-h).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1h and Figure 1—figure supplement 1f-h.

claim: DMOG most strongly upregulated both PLOD2 and LOXL2 mRNA and protein levels in primary human lung fibroblasts.
source: A prodrug form of the hypoxia mimetic and broad spectrum 2-oxoglutarate oxygenase inhibitor N-oxalylglycine (dimethyloxalylglycine, DMOG) (Chowdhury et al., 2013), which inhibits the HIF prolyl hydroxylases with consequent stabilisation of HIF1α and HIF2α, most strongly upregulated both PLOD2 and LOXL2 mRNA and protein levels (Figure 2a–c and Figure 2—figure supplement 1b)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a-c and Figure 2—figure supplement 1b.

claim: DMOG did not induce expression of interstitial collagen genes (COL1A1, COL3A1).
source: but did not induce expression of interstitial collagen genes (COL1A1, COL3A1) (Figure 2d and Figure 2—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2d and Figure 2—figure supplement 1c.

claim: TGFβ1 strongly induced COL1A1 and COL3A1 expression.
source: In contrast, TGFβ1 strongly induced COL1A1 and COL3A1 and this was associated with smaller up-regulation of PLOD2 at 24 hr and of LOXL2 at 72 hr (Figure 2a–d; Figure 2—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a-d and Figure 2—figure supplement 1c.

claim: TGFβ1 was associated with smaller up-regulation of PLOD2 at 24 hr and of LOXL2 at 72 hr.
source: In contrast, TGFβ1 strongly induced COL1A1 and COL3A1 and this was associated with smaller up-regulation of PLOD2 at 24 hr and of LOXL2 at 72 hr (Figure 2a–d; Figure 2—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a-d and Figure 2—figure supplement 1c.

claim: No induction of PLOD2 or LOXL2 was identified with canonical Wnt (Wnt3a), non-canonical Wnt (Wnt5a) or EGF pathway activation.
source: No induction of PLOD2 or LOXL2 was identified with canonical Wnt (Wnt3a), non-canonical Wnt (Wnt5a) or EGF pathway activation (Figure 2a–c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a-c.

claim: Treatment with the selective HIF prolyl 2 hydroxylase inhibitor IOX2 induced expression of PLOD2 and LOXL2.
source: We further extended these observations by showing that treatment with the selective HIF prolyl 2 hydroxylase inhibitor, N-[[1,2-dihydro-4-hydroxy-2-oxo-1-(phenylmethyl)–3-quinolinyl]carbonyl]-glycine (IOX2) (Chowdhury et al., 2013) or culture for 24 hr under hypoxic conditions induced expression of PLOD2 and LOXL2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d, e)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d, e.

claim: Culture for 24 hr under hypoxic conditions induced expression of PLOD2 and LOXL2.
source: We further extended these observations by showing that treatment with the selective HIF prolyl 2 hydroxylase inhibitor, N-[[1,2-dihydro-4-hydroxy-2-oxo-1-(phenylmethyl)–3-quinolinyl]carbonyl]-glycine (IOX2) (Chowdhury et al., 2013) or culture for 24 hr under hypoxic conditions induced expression of PLOD2 and LOXL2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d, e)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d, e.

claim: Immunofluorescent staining confirmed an increase in intracellular LOXL2 and PLOD2 expression following DMOG or IOX2 treatment in comparison to treatment with TGFβ1.
source: with immunofluorescent staining confirming an increase in intracellular LOXL2 and PLOD2 expression following DMOG or IOX2 treatment in comparison to treatment with TGFβ1 (Figure 2e).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: The knockdown of HIF1α prevented DMOG induction of PLOD2 mRNA and protein expression.
source: The knockdown of HIF1α, but not HIF2α prevented DMOG induction of PLOD2 mRNA and protein expression
evidence: The claim is supported by siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3b-d.

claim: The knockdown of HIF2α did not prevent DMOG induction of PLOD2 mRNA and protein expression.
source: The knockdown of HIF1α, but not HIF2α prevented DMOG induction of PLOD2 mRNA and protein expression
evidence: The claim is supported by siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3b-d.

claim: LOXL2 induction by DMOG required silencing of both HIF1α and HIF2α or HIF1β.
source: whilst LOXL2 required silencing of both HIF1α and HIF2α or HIF1β (Figure 3b–d).
evidence: The claim is supported by siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3b-d.

claim: HIF stabilisation is required to orchestrate induction of PLOD2 and LOXL2 expression in human lung fibroblasts.
source: Together, these findings identify that HIF stabilisation is required to orchestrate induction of PLOD2 and LOXL2 expression in human lung fibroblasts.
evidence: The claim is based on the siRNA knockdown experiments and HIF pathway activation studies.

claim: The combination of DMOG and TGFβ1 had a synergistic effect upon the induction of PLOD2 expression that was greater than either pathway alone.
source: When combined, a synergistic effect upon the induction of PLOD2 expression was apparent which was greater than either pathway alone (Figure 4a and c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a and c.

claim: Expression of LOXL2 was increased with the combination of HIF stabilisation and TGFβ1.
source: Whilst expression of LOXL2 was also increased with the combination of HIF stabilisation and TGFβ1, a corresponding increase in LOXL2 protein levels within cell lysates was not apparent.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations from the combination treatment studies.

claim: Under conditions with HIF stabilisation, LOXL2 secretion was increased in both IPF fibroblasts and control fibroblasts.
source: As LOXL2 is processed intracellularly before being extracellularly secreted, we therefore investigated whether increased secretion of LOXL2 was occurring; this identified that under conditions with HIF stabilisation LOXL2 secretion was increased in both IPF fibroblasts (Figure 4d) and control fibroblasts (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4d and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: HIF stabilisation significantly increased the ratio of PLOD2 and LOXL2 gene expression relative to fibrillar collagen (COL1A1) gene expression.
source: HIF stabilisation significantly increased the ratio of PLOD2 and LOXL2 gene expression relative to fibrillar collagen (COL1A1) gene expression while TGFβ1 did not (Figure 4e and f)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4e and f.

claim: TGFβ1 did not significantly increase the ratio of PLOD2 and LOXL2 gene expression relative to fibrillar collagen (COL1A1) gene expression.
source: HIF stabilisation significantly increased the ratio of PLOD2 and LOXL2 gene expression relative to fibrillar collagen (COL1A1) gene expression while TGFβ1 did not (Figure 4e and f)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4e and f.

claim: TGFβ activity alone may be insufficient to promote the altered collagen cross-linking that is present in IPF lung tissue.
source: suggesting that TGFβ activity alone may be insufficient to promote the altered collagen cross-linking that is present in IPF lung tissue.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the ratio analysis of PLOD2/LOXL2 to COL1A1 expression.

claim: TGFβ1 has a dominant role in increasing the rate of synthesis of major fibrillar collagens.
source: Together these findings demonstrate that whilst TGFβ1 has a dominant role in increasing the rate of synthesis of major fibrillar collagens, HIF pathways may have a key role in regulating pathological post-translational modifications and collagen structure in lung fibrosis.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental findings showing TGFβ1 strongly induces COL1A1 and COL3A1.

claim: HIF pathways may have a key role in regulating pathological post-translational modifications and collagen structure in lung fibrosis.
source: Together these findings demonstrate that whilst TGFβ1 has a dominant role in increasing the rate of synthesis of major fibrillar collagens, HIF pathways may have a key role in regulating pathological post-translational modifications and collagen structure in lung fibrosis.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental findings showing HIF pathway activation increases PLOD2/LOXL2 expression.

claim: Following 6 weeks of culture with TGFβ1 and IOX2, mature pyridinoline cross links (DPD/PYD) were significantly increased by the addition of IOX2.
source: Following 6 weeks of culture with TGFβ1 in the absence (control) or presence of IOX2 to drive HIF pathway activation, mature pyridinoline cross links (DPD/PYD) were significantly increased by the addition of IOX2 (Figure 5a)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the 3D model shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Pyridinoline cross-links following IOX2 treatment achieved a level comparable to previous findings in IPF tissue.
source: and these achieved a level comparable to our previous findings in IPF tissue (Jones et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim compares current findings to prior published data (Jones et al., 2018).

claim: IOX2 treatment resulted in a greater than threefold increase in tissue stiffness.
source: The biomechanical consequence of HIF stabilisation by IOX2 treatment was then investigated with parallel plate compression testing, identifying a greater than threefold increase in tissue stiffness by the addition of IOX2 (Figure 5b)
evidence: The claim is supported by biomechanical testing data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: The mean compressive modulus measurement following IOX2 treatment was (107.1 ± 10.7) kPa, comparable to the maximal stiffness of between 50 and 150 kPa previously identified in highly fibrotic areas in IPF tissue.
source: with the mean (± SEM) compressive modulus measurement following IOX2 treatment of (107.1 ± 10.7) kPa comparable to the maximal stiffness of between 50 and 150 kPa we and others have previously identified in highly fibrotic areas in IPF tissue (Booth et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim compares current findings to prior published data (Booth et al., 2012).

claim: Ultrastructural analysis of the collagen fibrils using electron microscopy identified a change in collagen nanostructure with a significant decrease in fibril diameter when pyridinoline cross-linking was increased by IOX2.
source: By contrast, ultrastructural analysis of the collagen fibrils using electron microscopy identified a change in collagen nanostructure with a significant decrease in fibril diameter (Figure 5d and e) when pyridinoline cross-linking was increased by IOX2
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5d and e.

claim: The decrease in fibril diameter with increased pyridinoline cross-linking is consistent with previous observations that fibril diameter is increased by inhibition of pyridinoline cross-linking.
source: consistent with our previous observation that fibril diameter is increased by inhibition of pyridinoline cross-linking (Jones et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim references prior published data (Jones et al., 2018) for consistency.

claim: Non-hydrated collagen fibrils from patients with IPF have reduced diameters when measured by atomic force microscopy.
source: In support of the disease relevance of our in vitro findings, non-hydrated collagen fibrils from patients with IPF have reduced diameters when measured by atomic force microscopy (Figure 5f)
evidence: The claim is supported by atomic force microscopy data shown in Figure 5f.

claim: Hydrated collagen fibrils extracted from IPF lung tissue have a reduced diameter compared to control samples.
source: consistent with our previous findings that hydrated collagen fibrils extracted from IPF lung tissue have a reduced diameter compared to control samples (Jones et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim references prior published data (Jones et al., 2018).

claim: HIF pathway activation is a key regulator of pyridinoline cross-link density, collagen fibril nano-architecture, and tissue stiffness.
source: Together, these data identify HIF pathway activation to be a key regulator of pyridinoline cross-link density, collagen fibril nano-architecture, and tissue stiffness.
evidence: The claim is based on the collective findings from the 3D model experiments.

claim: Elevated levels of HIF1α and HIF2α in IPF fibroblasts under normoxic conditions have recently been reported.
source: Whilst canonical HIF pathway activation was observed in lung fibroblasts under hypoxic conditions, elevated levels of HIF1α and HIF2α in IPF fibroblasts under normoxic conditions have recently been reported (Aquino-Gálvez et al., 2019)
evidence: The claim references a recent publication (Aquino-Gálvez et al., 2019).

claim: Fibroblasts cultured under normoxic conditions from patients with a usual interstitial pneumonia pattern of fibrosis or systemic sclerosis associated lung fibrosis have a significantly increased HIF score compared to cultured control fibroblasts.
source: To further investigate this possibility, we employed gene set variation analysis (GSVA) using a validated 15-gene HIF/hypoxia gene expression signature (Buffa et al., 2010) to published datasets, identifying that fibroblasts cultured under normoxic conditions from patients with a usual interstitial pneumonia pattern of fibrosis or systemic sclerosis associated lung fibrosis have a significantly increased HIF score (i.e. manifest evidence for HIF upregulation) compared to cultured control fibroblasts (Figure 6a)
evidence: The claim is supported by GSVA analysis of published datasets shown in Figure 6a.

claim: There was a significant increase in the HIF score in lung mesenchymal stromal cells of patients with progressive lung fibrosis compared to those with stable fibrosis.
source: Furthermore, there was a significant increase in the HIF score in lung mesenchymal stromal cells of patients with progressive lung fibrosis compared to those with stable fibrosis (Figure 6b)
evidence: The claim is supported by GSVA analysis shown in Figure 6b.

claim: HIF pathway activation may be required for fibrosis progression.
source: suggesting that HIF pathway activation may be required for fibrosis progression.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the HIF score analysis in progressive vs stable fibrosis.

claim: Loss of FIH was sufficient to induce both PLOD2 and LOXL2 expression under normoxic conditions.
source: Initially, to investigate the potential role of reduced FIH activity in regulating collagen post-translational modifications, we silenced FIH under normoxic conditions; the results show that loss of FIH was sufficient to induce both PLOD2 and LOXL2 expression
evidence: The claim is supported by siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 6c.

claim: The induction of PLOD2 and LOXL2 by FIH knockdown required HIF promoted transcription, since HIF1β knockdown prevented their induction.
source: and that this effect required HIF promoted transcription, since HIF1β knockdown prevented their induction (Figure 6c).
evidence: The claim is supported by siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 6c.

claim: FIH activity was significantly reduced in fibroblasts from patients with IPF compared to control fibroblasts.
source: Consistent with a loss of function of FIH in lung fibrosis, we found FIH activity was significantly reduced in fibroblasts from patients with IPF compared to control fibroblasts (Figure 6e).
evidence: The claim is supported by HIF1α CAD reporter assay data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: A reduction in FIH activity in normal lung fibroblasts could be caused under normoxia by oxidative stress, achieving a level of HIF CAD activity comparable to treatment with the hypoxia mimetic DMOG.
source: We further confirmed that a reduction in FIH activity in normal lung fibroblasts could be caused under normoxia by oxidative stress, achieving a level of HIF CAD activity comparable to treatment with the hypoxia mimetic DMOG (Figure 6f).
evidence: The claim is supported by HIF1α CAD reporter assay data shown in Figure 6f.

claim: In lung fibroblasts a reduction in FIH activity may promote HIF pathway activation to dysregulate collagen structure-function.
source: Thus, in lung fibroblasts a reduction in FIH activity may promote HIF pathway activation to dysregulate collagen structure-function.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the FIH activity and knockdown experiments.

claim: FIH inhibition by DM-NOFD was sufficient to induce the HIF pathway activation marker gene carbonic anhydrase IX (CA9), PLOD2, and LOXL2 gene expression following 2-week culture.
source: We confirmed that FIH inhibition by DM-NOFD was sufficient to induce the HIF pathway activation marker gene carbonic anhydrase IX (CA9), PLOD2, and LOXL2 gene expression following 2-week culture (Figure 6—figure supplement 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Following 6 weeks of culture, DM-NOFD increased mature pyridinoline cross-links.
source: Following 6 weeks of culture, DM-NOFD increased mature pyridinoline cross-links (Figure 6g)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the 3D model shown in Figure 6g.

claim: DM-NOFD increased tissue stiffness following 6 weeks of culture.
source: as well as tissue stiffness (Figure 6h)
evidence: The claim is supported by biomechanical testing data shown in Figure 6h.

claim: The combination of DM-NOFD and IOX2 was additive in increasing pyridinoline cross-links and tissue stiffness.
source: whilst the combination of DM-NOFD and IOX2 was additive.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the 3D model with combination treatment.

claim: FIH inhibition can promote collagen post-translational modification and increase tissue stiffness.
source: Thus, FIH inhibition can promote collagen post-translational modification and increase tissue stiffness.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental findings with DM-NOFD treatment.

claim: The HIF signature score, but not TGFβ score, significantly correlated with LOXL2/PLOD2 expression in fibroblast foci.
source: To assess for HIF activity, we applied GSVA using the 15-gene HIF/hypoxia gene expression signature (Buffa et al., 2010) to the transcriptome of each fibroblast focus, identifying that the HIF signature score, but not TGFβ score, significantly correlated with LOXL2/PLOD2 expression (Figure 7a and b).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSVA analysis shown in Figure 7a and b.

claim: HIF1α and the HIF pathway activation marker gene carbonic anhydrase IX (CA-IX) were expressed within fibroblast foci.
source: Furthermore, analysis of serial tissue sections using immunohistochemistry identified that HIF1α and the HIF pathway activation marker gene carbonic anhydrase IX (CA-IX) were expressed within fibroblast foci (Bodempudi et al., 2014; Loncaster et al., 2001)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7c and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: HIF1α and CA-IX expression localised to cells co-expressing LOXL2 and PLOD2 mRNA in fibroblast foci.
source: and that this expression localised to cells co-expressing LOXL2 and PLOD2 mRNA (Figure 7c; Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry and RNA in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 7c and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Compared to fibroblasts and myofibroblasts, the HAS1 high and PLIN2+ cells had significantly increased HIF and upregulated oxidative stress scores.
source: Applying HIF signature or upregulated oxidative stress gene expression signatures to this dataset, we identified that, compared to fibroblasts and myofibroblasts, the HAS1 high and PLIN2+ cells, whose presence was almost exclusively derived from the IPF lung tissue, had significantly increased HIF and upregulated oxidative stress scores (Figure 8a–d)
evidence: The claim is supported by GSVA analysis of single cell RNAseq data shown in Figure 8a-d.

claim: HIF and upregulated oxidative stress scores were significantly correlated in HAS1 high and PLIN2+ cells.
source: and that these two scores were significantly correlated (Figure 8e)
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 8e.

claim: The correlation between HIF and oxidative stress scores is consistent with an increase in pseudohypoxic HIF activity in disease-specific mesenchymal cell types.
source: consistent with an increase in pseudohypoxic HIF activity in these disease-specific mesenchymal cell types.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the correlation analysis.

claim: HIF pathway activation promotes pathologic pyridinoline collagen crosslinking and tissue stiffness by disproportionate induction of collagen-modifying enzymes relative to TGFβ-induced collagen fibril synthesis.
source: Here, through ex vivo models, bioinformatics and human lung fibrosis tissue studies, we extend these observations leading to the discovery that HIF pathway activation promotes pathologic pyridinlone collagen crosslinking and tissue stiffness by disproportionate induction of collagen-modifying enzymes relative to TGFβ-induced collagen fibril synthesis.
evidence: The claim is based on the collective findings from the study.

claim: Pseudohypoxic oxygen-independent HIF activation may occur via a decrease in FIH activity that can occur due to oxidative stress.
source: Furthermore, this may occur via pseudohypoxic oxygen-independent mechanisms, including the involvement of a decrease in FIH activity that can occur due to oxidative stress, which is thought to play a significant role in IPF pathogenesis (Cheresh et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is based on the FIH activity experiments and references prior literature on oxidative stress in IPF.

claim: Oxidative stress is increased in subpopulations of IPF fibroblasts.
source: Consistent with this, oxidative stress is increased in subpopulations of IPF fibroblasts
evidence: The claim is based on the GSVA analysis of single cell RNAseq data.

claim: FIH activity is significantly reduced in fibroblasts from patients with lung fibrosis resulting in HIF activation under normoxic conditions.
source: whilst FIH activity is significantly reduced in fibroblasts from patients with lung fibrosis resulting in HIF activation under normoxic conditions.
evidence: The claim is based on the HIF1α CAD reporter assay data.

claim: Dysregulated HIF activity is a core regulator of ECM structure-function in human lung fibrosis.
source: Thus, we provide evidence that dysregulated HIF activity is a core regulator of ECM structure-function in human lung fibrosis
evidence: The claim is based on the collective findings from the study.

claim: Dysregulated HIF activity may be a key determinant of pathologic tissue stiffness and progressive human lung fibrosis.
source: and that this may be a key determinant of pathologic tissue stiffness and progressive human lung fibrosis.
evidence: The claim is based on the collective findings from the study.

claim: TGFβ is a multifunctional growth factor with key roles in normal development and wound healing.
source: TGFβ is a multifunctional growth factor with key roles in normal development and wound healing.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about TGFβ.

claim: TGFβ is considered the prototypic profibrogenic cytokine that promotes increased ECM deposition and has been associated with fibrosis across multiple organs.
source: It is also considered the prototypic profibrogenic cytokine that promotes increased ECM deposition and has been associated with fibrosis across multiple organs (Yue et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim references prior literature (Yue et al., 2010).

claim: TGFβ pathway activation alone may be insufficient to cause a substantial increase in pathologic pyridinoline collagen crosslinking.
source: We identified that in lung fibroblasts, TGFβ1 increased fibrillar collagen mRNA transcription but its relative effects on PLOD2 or LOXL2 were more limited, suggesting that TGFβ pathway activation alone may be insufficient to cause a substantial increase in pathologic pyridinoline collagen crosslinking.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental findings.

claim: HIF-mediated transcription appears to be relatively more important in inducing PLOD2/LOXL2 relative to interstitial collagen fibril synthesis.
source: HIF-mediated transcription appears to be relatively more important in inducing PLOD2/LOXL2 relative to interstitial collagen fibril synthesis, so promoting pyridinoline collagen cross-linking, altering collagen fibril nanostructure, and increasing tissue stiffness.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental findings.

claim: TGFβ has been reported to cause HIF stabilisation.
source: While TGFβ has been reported to cause HIF stabilisation (Basu et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim references prior literature (Basu et al., 2011).

claim: The effect of TGFβ on HIF stabilisation is modest and further HIF-mediated activation is likely required to drive matrix stiffening.
source: our findings suggest that this effect is modest and that further HIF-mediated activation is likely required to drive matrix stiffening.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental findings.

claim: HIF proteins play a relatively important role in the induction of PLOD2 expression compared to TGFβ stimulated SMAD proteins.
source: This proposal is consistent with a recent result implying a hierarchical relationship in which HIF proteins play a relatively important role in the induction of PLOD2 expression, that is in this regard the effect of the HIF transcription factors appears to be more important relative to that of TGFβ stimulated SMAD proteins (Rosell-García et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim references prior literature (Rosell-García et al., 2019).

claim: HIF pathway activation acts as a key pathologic 'second hit' which disrupts the normal wound healing role of TGFβ by altering collagen fibril nanoarchitecture so dysregulating ECM structure-function and promoting progressive lung fibrosis.
source: Thus, we propose that HIF pathway activation acts as a key pathologic 'second hit' which disrupts the normal wound healing role of TGFβ by altering collagen fibril nanoarchitecture so dysregulating ECM structure-function and promoting progressive lung fibrosis.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the collective findings.

claim: HIF activity was increased in cells from patients with progressive lung fibrosis compared with those with stable disease.
source: In keeping with this concept, GSVA using a validated HIF score (Buffa et al., 2010) applied to microarray data for lung mesenchymal stromal cells showed that HIF activity was increased in cells from patients with progressive lung fibrosis compared with those with stable disease.
evidence: The claim is based on GSVA analysis of published data.

claim: HIF pathway activation using a HIF stabilising PHD inhibitor and/or an FIH inhibitor increased pyridinoline cross-links to a level comparable to that identified in IPF tissue.
source: We investigated the functional consequences of our findings by employing our long-term 3D in vitro model of lung fibrosis. The results show that HIF pathway activation using a HIF stabilising PHD inhibitor and/or an FIH inhibitor increased pyridinoline cross-links to a level comparable to that identified in IPF tissue
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the 3D model.

claim: The increase in cross-links is associated with an increase in tissue stiffness comparable to the extremes of stiffness identified in IPF tissue.
source: and that the increase in cross-links is associated with an increase in tissue stiffness comparable to the extremes of stiffness identified in IPF tissue
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the 3D model.

claim: The increase in cross-links is associated with a reduction in fibril diameter similar to those present in IPF lung tissue.
source: together with a reduction in fibril diameter similar to those present in IPF lung tissue.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from the 3D model.

claim: The 3D in vitro model recapitulates key features of dysregulated collagen structure-function in IPF.
source: Together these observations support the human disease relevance of HIF pathway activation to IPF and define conditions for future mechanistic studies whereby the 3D in vitro model recapitulates key features of dysregulated collagen structure-function in IPF.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the 3D model findings.

claim: LOXL2 was the most highly expressed LOX/LOXL family member in LCMD RNA-Seq analyses.
source: In our LCMD RNA-Seq analyses, LOXL2 was the most highly expressed LOX/LOXL family member
evidence: The claim is based on LCMD RNA-Seq data.

claim: LOXL2 was the only LOX/LOXL member which correlated with PLOD2 expression in LCMD RNA-Seq analyses.
source: as well as the only LOX/LOXL member which correlated with PLOD2 expression
evidence: The claim is based on LCMD RNA-Seq data.

claim: Gene expression of LOXL2 was significantly increased in IPF tissue when compared to age-matched control lung tissue.
source: whilst in our previous work investigating collagen structure-function dysregulation in human lung fibrosis, we identified that gene expression of LOXL2 was significantly increased in IPF tissue when compared to age-matched control lung tissue (Jones et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim references prior published data (Jones et al., 2018).

claim: Using a small molecule LOXL inhibitor in the 3D model of fibrosis, there was a greater than 50% reduction in mature pyridinoline cross-links using a concentration which completely inhibits LOXL2 but has minimal effects on LOX and LOXL1.
source: Furthermore, using a small molecule LOXL inhibitor in our 3D model of fibrosis, we identified a greater than 50% reduction in mature pyridinoline cross-links using a concentration which completely inhibits LOXL2 but has minimal effects on LOX and LOXL1 (Jones et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim references prior published data (Jones et al., 2018).

claim: LOXL2 has key pathologic roles in cancer and fibrosis.
source: This is consistent with previous reports that LOXL2 has key pathologic roles in cancer and fibrosis (Barker et al., 2012; Barry-Hamilton et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim references prior literature (Barker et al., 2012; Barry-Hamilton et al., 2010).

claim: The HIF signalling pathway has been reported to be active in lungs and fibroblasts from IPF patients, as determined by the abundance of HIF1α and HIF2α.
